title: Ask Curator: Signal Notes & Curation Journal (Jun 2027)
content:
Purpose / framing:
This note is a compact working journal for the customer-success + solutions handoff: capture the persistent runtime/behavior signals seen in the last 8 weeks, group them by actionable theme, and surface low-effort/high-risk items for engineering to triage. Intention is to keep this informal — a curated scrapbook to feed the next triage sync (CS <> Eng, 2027-06-03).

Quick synopsis (topline):
- We continue to see 3 recurring customer asks that drive tickets and churn risk: (1) KV cache invalidation surprises for multi-tenant prompts, (2) inconsistent latency spikes when batch sizes change, (3) embedding rerank quality drift after upgrade to v2 quantized models.
- Rough impact signals: repeated field escalations (~12 unique customers in last 6 weeks), ~8 ship-stopping bug threads created, and several customers experimenting with conservative TTLs and disabled caching as temporary mitigations (cost up ~15% for those customers).

Representative voice snippets (actual paraphrased customer quotes):
- "Our assistant starts repeating previous user context when two users share similar prefixes — we thought we were isolated; now we have leakage-like behavior." — enterprise search customer
- "When we increase batch size from 8 to 16 for throughput, p50 is fine but p95 jumps ~250ms and we see more 503s — unsure if it's model warmup or queueing misconfig." — fintech client
- "After the new quantized r2 models rolled out, our reranking scores change subtly and our A/B conversion dropped 3% — we need a way to compare the ranking space side-by-side." — content platform

Thematic curation (grouped asks + evidence):
1) KV cache semantics and isolation
   Evidence: 6 support threads (IDs: JIRA-4521, JIRA-4608) describing context carryover; two customers reproduced locally with sequence-level KV replays; one reproduction shows cache not being flushed when switching tenant keys on pooled hosts.
   Customer cost workaround: increased cache TTL to 0 (disabled) or added synthetic namespace token to prompts.
   Impact: correctness + compliance risk for enterprise customers; some have paused private deployments until semantics are clearer.
   Suggested probe: small canary change to instrumentation (add per-request cache-key log, expose debug flag to CS) + short-run test in dedicated pool to reproduce isolation boundary.

2) Batch-size-induced p95 latency spikes
   Evidence: field telemetry (internal console traces) indicating p50 stable, p95 and p99 correlated to batch size boundary crossing; reproductions show queueing/packing overhead + GPU kernel scheduling jitter.
   Customer workaround: conservative batching (smaller batches) leading to higher unit cost.
   Impact: Bad for customers optimizing throughput/cost trade-offs.
   Suggested probe: triage with serving-runtime team; identify if packing algorithm treats heterogeneous sequence lengths suboptimally. Quick experiment: add a phase where batch-builder prefers length-homogeneous packing for one-minute windows and observe tail latency.

3) Embeddings / reranking drift after quantized model rollouts
   Evidence: multiple customer A/B experiments show small but meaningful ranking differences; internal ML team notes small numeric shifts in embedding L2 norms after quantization.
   Customer workaround: pin older float model or recalibrate similarity thresholds per-customer.
   Impact: product metrics (CTR, relevance) for search/rerank customers.
   Suggested probe: build a small comparison harness (off-prod) to compute embedding drift metrics per-candidate set and flag customers with >threshold change and propose per-customer rollback.

Lower-effort/high-leverage patches (quick wins we can try in 2-4 weeks):
- Expose a labelled toggle in Console: "strict-kv-isolation-mode" (feature flag restricted to tiered accounts) — SCT: product + eng to scope UX and safe defaults (JIRA-4723).
- Add a telemetry breadcrumb to logs when cache hit/miss for requests flagged by CS (low perf risk, no customer-visible change).
- Run a short (1-week) internal benchmark comparing batching heuristics with sequence-length-aware packer; if tail improves, make it opt-in for Dedicated customers.

Engineering blockers and unknowns (things that need deeper investigation):
- We don't have a canonical repro for the tenant-key leakage on pooled hosts that includes network-level orchestration; requires SRE + serving-runtime alignment.
- Impact of quantization across model families is not uniform; need research tradeoffs (quality delta vs cost savings) per family.
- Metrics: we lack per-customer similarity drift thresholds to automate alerts — product/ML should propose a signal metric.

Risk matrix (simple):
- High risk / high visibility: KV isolation bug (legal/regulatory exposure) — mitigation: high-priority debug traces + limited rollback plan.
- Medium risk: Batch tail latency vs throughput tradeoffs — mitigation: opt-in packing experiments + per-customer knobs.
- Low risk / high skill required: embedding distribution drift — mitigation: put on research backlog but provide CS with guidance for pinning models.

Prioritization recommendation (CS POV):
- Rank 1: KV isolation investigation (stopgap: toggle + logs) — owner: Tessa + Lina (CS), eng owner requested: Priya (serving-runtime).
- Rank 2: Batch tail experiment (trial opt-in) — owner: Ari (solutions eng), eng owner requested: Mateo (runtime).
- Rank 3: Embedding drift harness (research spike then operationalize) — owner: Noah (product-ops), eng/ML owner: Sasha (applied-ml).

Concrete next steps (short horizon to sync):
- 2027-06-01: Share this doc and run 30-minute spike with serving-runtime to confirm log changes we can add without SLA risk (owner: Tessa).
- 2027-06-03: CS <> Eng triage sync; agenda: reproduce KV leak, define experiment for batching, scope embedding-harness (owner: Lina to set invite + attach artifacts).
- Assign quick JIRA tickets for each quick-win: JIRA-4723 (flag), JIRA-4731 (telemetry breadcrumbs), JIRA-4740 (packing experiment).

Open questions for triage meeting (bring data):
- Which dedicated pools share host-level resources across tenants (SRE input needed)?
- Can runtime add ephemeral per-request context IDs in logs for a short window without PII leakage?
- How large is the embedding numeric shift (distribution summary) after quantization across the top-5 models; can we threshold it?

Appendix (field reproduction notes):
- Repro notes for KV scenario: customer A (tenant-x) provided a trimmed trace where switching API-key on same connection resulted in repeated past prompt insertion at token idx ~+9. Reproduction steps attached in linked artifact (JIRA-4521).
- Batch repro: internal test harness (bench-v2) shows p95 increase ~220ms when mixing 64/512 sequence lengths in same packing window; suggested short-term workaround: prefer length-bucketing.

Unresolved items to capture in Confluence:
- Proposed doc: "KV isolation semantics — expected behaviors and failcases" (owner: Lina) — to be created by 2027-06-07.
- Short playbook for CS: how to safely recommend toggles vs pinning models to customers.

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Keep this doc lightweight and iterative; will push final summary into Confluence after June triage.
- Add a small checklist for ship conditions if we change cache defaults (audit, migration plan, communication templates).

---
End of journal entry.
